This is followed by a transition phase for which the formulas outlined in section 2.2 above do not apply. Therefore, different methods were needed to characterize the physical dimensions of the changing plume and to calculate the plume concentration during the transition period to allow for a smooth transition from the end of the dense gas phase to the neutrally buoyant phase. 2.3.1 Modification of Gaussian Dispersion Coefficients EPIcode uses the Gaussian Atmospheric Dispersion equations to characterize a dispersing plume during typical neutrally buoyant conditions. These equations use parameterized values to describe turbulence known as the Gaussian Dispersion Coefficients in the horizontal ( ) and y , vertical ( ) directions. z For the transition phase, the EPIcode model incorporated methods from Van Ulden (1974), which are based on these same Gaussian dispersion coefficients. In early studies of dense gas dispersion, it was observed that the vertical dispersion of the gas was diminished, and the horizontal dispersion was enhanced.
